keepalive.off: Keep alive is off for this provider.

quota.planTitleHint: The query plan this provider uses to read quota
quota.settingsDesc: How Nestra reads quota for this provider and keeps it fresh.
quota.planNoneHint: No query configured — quota display, auto-refresh, and keep-alive stay off until you pick one.
quota.verified: Query verified — quota + auto-refresh + keep-alive unlocked.
quota.notVerified: Query selected but not yet verified — click “verify query” (or Test in the custom form) to confirm data.
quota.previewHint: Only enabled windows show on the provider card preview.
quota.autoHintOn: Refresh the quota bars on a timer while this window is open.
quota.autoHintOff: Verify the query first to enable auto-refresh.
quota.keepAliveLocked: Select a query plan first to unlock keep-alive.
quota.keepAliveUnverified: Worker verifies the query on its first tick — keep-alive can be armed now, or click “verify query” to confirm data first.
quota.keepAliveHint: Sends a tiny background ping when the target window expires.
quota.resetting: resetting — waiting for provider to clear the window
quota.armed: armed; ping fires when the target window expires
quota.verifyToSee: Verify the query to see quota.
quota.configureToSee: Configure a query plan to see quota.
quota.jsonPathHint: JSON path extraction: data.balance.0 = object data → array balance → index 0. Numbers, string numbers and [amount, "CNY"] money arrays are accepted. {{baseUrl}} / {{apiKey}} work in url and headers. No filtering, arithmetic or multi-window extraction — pick a single balance shape.
quota.credsHint: OpenCode Go has no API-key usage endpoint — Nestra reads the dashboard the same way the community tools do. Sign in at opencode.ai (GitHub / Google), then: workspace ID = the {id} in opencode.ai/workspace/{id}/go; cookie = your browser's auth cookie for opencode.ai (devtools → Application → Cookies). Re-paste when the session expires.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.noneFoundHint: Sessions are read from each coding agent's local logs (e.g. ~/.claude).
sessions.emptyDetail: Select a session to view its conversation.
sessions.deleteConfirmBody_one: This removes the session from Nestra AND deletes the source files from disk. The original agent will no longer be able to resume it.
sessions.deleteConfirmBody_other: This removes the sessions from Nestra AND deletes the source files from disk. The original agent will no longer be able to resume them.
sessions.deleteDetailBody: This removes it from Nestra AND deletes the source files from disk. The original agent will no longer be able to resume it.
sessions.openTip: Open this session in its native agent
sessions.revealTip: Reveal the session's source file in File Explorer
sessions.deleteTip: Delete this session (DB row + source files on disk)
sessions.handoffDialogDesc: Edit before saving — this markdown is what the next session reads.
sessions.handoffDeleteBody: Removes the handoff from Nestra's index. The markdown file stays on disk.
sessions.handoffSpawnTip: Open a new supervised Pi session seeded with this handoff

skills.title: Skills
skills.help: One canonical copy per skill, synced into each agent's skills dir. Toggle an agent to install or remove the skill from its folder.
skills.importableHint: Skills in agent folders Nestra isn't managing — import them.
skills.managedHint: Install a skill to manage it here.
skills.cardDesc: Toggle an agent to install the skill. Uninstall removes it from Nestra and every agent it's enabled for.
skills.unmanageTitle: Stop managing this skill in Nestra. The skill files stay in your agents' skill dirs (it keeps working) and it moves to Importable.
skills.unmanageConfirmBody: Nestra will no longer manage this skill. The skill files are left in your agents' skill dirs (they keep working) and it appears under Importable. This is the opposite of Uninstall, which removes them.
skills.uninstallConfirmBody: This removes the skill from Nestra and every agent it's enabled for.

mcp.title: MCP Servers
mcp.help: One canonical copy per server, synced into each agent's config. Hand-edited servers in CLI config files are left alone — import them to take over.
mcp.syncAllTitle: Re-project every managed server into every connected agent's config
mcp.noServersHint: Add one, or import one found in a CLI config.
mcp.serversDesc: Per agent: enabled (●), written but disabled (◐), or not written (○). Click a name to edit. Delete removes the server from Nestra and every agent.
mcp.restoreTitle: Stop managing this server in Nestra. The entries in your agents' config files stay (it keeps working) and it moves to Importable.
mcp.restoreConfirmBody: Nestra will no longer manage this server. The entry is left in your agents' config files (it keeps working) and appears under Importable. This is the opposite of Delete, which also removes the entries.
mcp.deleteConfirmBody: Removes the server from Nestra and every agent's config.
mcp.testTitle: Spin up the server's transport and check it answers
mcp.importScanHint: No MCP servers were found in your agents' config files outside Nestra's management.
mcp.importableDesc: MCP servers found in agent configs but not managed by Nestra yet. A server installed for several agents is shown once; Import enables it on all of them. Entries found with `enabled: false` stay disabled after import.
mcp.dialogDesc: Stored in Nestra's DB, then synced into the agents you enable. The global env applies to every agent; per-agent overrides layer on top.
mcp.name: Name
mcp.importScanFailed: Failed to scan for importable servers.

settings.title: Settings
settings.help: App-level preferences. Detection cadence and log retention apply across every agent and provider.
settings.autostartDesc: Start Nestra automatically when you sign in to the computer.
settings.appearanceDesc: The top-bar toggle switches light and dark; this controls whether the app follows your OS.
settings.themeDesc: System follows the OS preference; light/dark pin the theme.
settings.languageDesc: UI language — strings without a translation fall back to English.
settings.detectionDesc: When Nestra looks for installed agents on this machine.
settings.cadenceDesc: Scan for installed binaries on launch, or only when you trigger a manual re-scan.
settings.cadenceLaunchTip: Scan for installed agents when the app starts
settings.cadenceManualTip: Only when you trigger a re-scan
settings.logsDesc: How long Nestra keeps its own operational logs.
settings.retentionDesc: Older entries are pruned automatically. Diagnostics exports the current window.
settings.dataDesc: Whether the app restores the last loaded data instantly on relaunch (then refreshes in the background).
settings.keepDataDesc: Saves the data cache to local storage so pages show content immediately instead of a loading state.
settings.onTip: Restore the last data on relaunch, then refresh in the background
settings.cacheDesc: Cached data (model catalog, quota snapshots, page data) is rebuilt automatically. This only drops the cached copies.
settings.clearCachesDesc: Removes cached page data, quota snapshots, and the models.dev catalog. Providers, keys and sessions are untouched.
settings.clearConfirmBody: Drops the in-memory data cache, the persisted data cache, the quota snapshots, and the models.dev catalog cache. Data is re-fetched from disk and the network as needed — your providers, keys and sessions are untouched.
settings.diagSystemDesc: Where Nestra lives on this machine.
settings.diagOpenFailed: Could not open the data location: {{err}}
settings.diagAboutBody: Nestra is a unified control center for AI coding agents. Local-only — no cloud, no account. API keys are encrypted at rest.
settings.updatesDesc: Check GitHub for a newer version. Downloading and installing happens on the release page.
settings.updatesAvailableDesc: Open the release page to download the installer.
settings.updatesNoRelease: No release published yet on GitHub.
settings.updatesOpenFailed: Could not open the release page: {{err}}
settings.gatewayTuningDesc: Operational hardening for the routed path — applies to the next request, no gateway restart needed.
settings.gatewayTuningInfo: Timeouts bound each upstream phase (headers, first stream event, mid-stream silence, buffered body) plus the whole retry/migrate loop. The breaker excludes an endpoint after repeated failures and probes it again after the recovery wait. 0 disables the silence timeout and the error-rate backstop.
settings.gatewayTuning_headersHint: Upstream must send response headers within this. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_firstEventHint: First complete SSE event after headers. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_silenceHint: Max gap between stream frames mid-stream; 0 disables. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_bufferedHint: Total time to read a non-streaming body. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_deadlineHint: Hard wall-clock cap on retries+migrations per request. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_thresholdHint: Consecutive failures that open the breaker. {{min}}–{{max}}.
settings.gatewayTuning_recoveryHint: Open breaker waits this long before probe requests. {{min}}–{{max}}s.
settings.gatewayTuning_successHint: Consecutive successes that close the breaker. {{min}}–{{max}}.
settings.gatewayTuning_minRequestsHint: Window samples required before the error-rate backstop fires. {{min}}–{{max}}.
settings.gatewayTuningSavedToast: Gateway tuning saved — applies to the next request
settings.licensesDesc: Nestra is built on open-source software.

providers.title: Providers
providers.help: An LLM provider + API key per upstream. Each CLI binds to one provider at a time. Routing policy and fallback chains are configured per agent on the Agents page.
providers.keyRejected: Key rejected — finish setup on the edit page
providers.keyRejectedWith: Key rejected — finish setup on the edit page: {{msg}}
providers.protocolsFailed: Could not add {{n}} preset protocol(s) — add manually in the edit page.

none.title: No LLM providers configured
none.hint: Add one per upstream; Nestra manages the provider and its key.

providers.dialogDesc: Pick a preset and paste your key — validated in one step. Or go custom.
providers.customHint: Add protocol + base URL on the detail page after creating.
providers.breakerOpenTip: Endpoint excluded from routing after repeated failures ({{class}}); probe requests resume in {{secs}}s.
providers.breakerHalfOpenTip: Recovery wait elapsed — probe requests are flowing; consecutive successes close the circuit.
providers.healthResetToast: Provider health reset — all endpoints eligible again

agents.title: Agents
agents.help: Installed coding agents. Each agent runs in Direct mode (writes the real provider into its config) or Routed mode (traffic flows through the Nestra gateway — resolved per task, with quota-aware fallback). Open an agent for full configuration.
agents.toggleEnabled: {{name}} enabled — Nestra will write its config

none.title: No agents detected
none.hint: Install Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, or ZCode, then click Re-detect.

agents.installHint: install to enable switching, or pin a path manually
agents.managingDesc: Nestra is managing this agent's config
agents.leavingDesc: Nestra leaves this agent's config alone
agents.noCompatProviders: No compatible providers configured with an API key — add one on the Providers page.
agents.writeSelection: Write the current selection to this agent's config
agents.noConfigYet: No config file yet — it appears after the first provider switch.
agents.previewDialogDesc: Live preview of the agent's config file.
agents.disabledNote: Toggle the switch above to manage this agent's provider/connector configuration.
agents.wirePickerTitle: Which API wire this agent speaks to the provider

orchestration.roleHeuristic: no metadata — role defaulted heuristically to Main
orchestration.stateAbsent: not written to this agent's config
orchestration.modeRoutedToast: Now routing via the Nestra gateway
orchestration.modeBlockedHint: Enable the Gateway service on the Gateway page to route this agent.
orchestration.modeLoadFailed: Mode setting failed to load — retry.

agentRouting.help: Policies map (agent, role) → preferred / fallback / allowed models. The gateway resolves each request: explicit → affinity → capability → fail closed.
agentRouting.steadyHint: What a new request resolves to under the current policies — a dry-run, no traffic sent. Updates when you save a policy.
agentRouting.steadyNoRoute: no eligible route — check provider health/quota and the policy's allowed models
agentRouting.policyHint: (agent, role) → preferred / fallback / allowed models · match order: exact role → tier:* → *
agentRouting.gateTitle: routing policy is a Routed-mode surface
agentRouting.gateHint: This agent is in Direct mode — its config is written as a plain provider binding. Switch to Routed to configure (agent, role) → provider chain policies.
agentRouting.directNote: This agent is in Direct mode right now — policies take effect the moment you switch to Routed. Editing here is safe.

agentDetail.helpGateway: Direct mode writes the real provider into this agent's config. Routed mode sends traffic through the Nestra gateway — provider/model resolved per task, with quota-aware fallback and migration.
agentDetail.policyHint: (agent, role) → preferred / fallback / allowed models · match order: exact role → tier:* → *
agentDetail.detectedRolesHint: subagent roles seen on routed requests · edit policies on the routing page
agentDetail.noGatewayTrafficHint: Once this agent is routed and a request flows through, each task appears here with its full route lineage: requested model → resolved provider, route reason, prompt-cache metrics, and generation-broken flags.
agentDetail.reviewHint: Spawn isolated review sessions on finished work
agentDetail.usageHint: gateway-observed tokens, last 30 days · spend priced live from the model catalog
agentDetail.directHint: Nestra writes the real provider into the agent's config; it talks straight to the bound endpoint.
agentDetail.routingCardHint: Role policies decide where the gateway sends each request.
agentDetail.policyEmpty: no route targets — routing fails closed
agentDetail.usageEmptyHint: Usage appears once requests flow through the gateway.

routingPolicy.noPolicies: No policies saved — routing is fail-closed until the * policy has targets.
routingPolicy.configuredTip: Policy already configured for this role
routingPolicy.tierTip: Create a policy for {{role}} — matches requests Claude Code sends through that model slot (lookup order: exact role, then tier, then *). Useful to steer background traffic to a cheaper provider.
routingPolicy.addRoleHint: Use * for catch-all, or a SubagentRole key (main, claude:{name}, pi:{role}, opencode:{name})
routingPolicy.migrateOnQuotaDesc: Move to a fallback when quota/rate-limit hits.
routingPolicy.affinityTaskTip: per-task affinity — reuse the previous route within one task, which protects the prompt cache
routingPolicy.affinitySessionTip: session affinity — reuse the route across the whole logical session
routingPolicy.affinityNoneTip: no affinity — route from scratch every request
routingPolicy.targetsHint: Ordered (provider, model) pins — the router serves the first healthy entry; quota/5xx failures walk down the list.
routingPolicy.targetsEmpty: No targets — routing fails closed for this role until one is added.

providerEdit.validationError: {{err}} — fix the field and click Save again.
providerEdit.dangerHint: Removes the provider and deletes its API key from the OS keychain.
providerEdit.deleteConfirmHasKey: This removes its API key from the OS keychain.
providerEdit.deleteConfirmNoKey: This removes the provider from Nestra.
providerEdit.name: Name
providerEdit.nameHint: Shown across Nestra + written into agent configs.
providerEdit.protocolsHint: Which wire protocols this upstream speaks — drives URL + auth header. App picks the matching one when switching into an agent.
providerEdit.noProtocols: no protocols yet — add one below
providerEdit.protoCustomDesc: Your own endpoint — picked for Custom providers
providerEdit.modelsHint: Default model is required. Tiers fall back to default if blank — leave blank if the agent doesn't need explicit tier overrides.
providerEdit.perModelCapsDesc: Reasoning / tool-call / attachment flags OpenCode reads per-model. Defaults come from models.dev; toggle a field to set an override.
providerEdit.apiResponsesTip: Responses API — Direct mode excludes this model; use Routed mode (gateway converts)
providerEdit.apiOpenaiTip: OpenAI Chat Completions — excluded from Anthropic-protocol Direct binds
providerEdit.resetOverridesTip: Clear every override for this model — all fields inherit the default again
providerEdit.noDefaultOn: no default — toggle on to set
providerEdit.apiKeyHint: Validated by trying each protocol — nothing is persisted until validation succeeds.
providerEdit.advancedEnvHint: Extra keys merged into env-style agents (Claude Code). Stringified on write.
providerEdit.configPreviewDesc: What Nestra writes into each CLI's config when this provider is active. Key redacted.

gateway.title: Gateway Service
gateway.help: The local Gateway Service routes agent requests through Nestra. Enable it, then opt agents in on their routing page.
gateway.disabledToast: Gateway disabled — routed agents reverted to Direct
gateway.partialFailToast: Gateway updated, but some agents could not be reconfigured: {{agents}}
gateway.autopickToast: Bound to first free loopback port {{port}}
gateway.runtimeCardDesc: Live gateway process state and bound endpoint.
gateway.portHint: A busy port surfaces an error; use Auto-pick to find the next free port.
gateway.tokenCardDesc: Agents must present this token; the gateway rejects unauthenticated requests.
gateway.tokenHint: Required — stored encrypted in the keychain, never in the database.
gateway.regenConfirmBody: All routed agents will be reconfigured. In-flight requests may be rejected until their config updates.
gateway.agentsCardDesc: Agents opted into gateway routing (intent preserved when the gateway is off).
gateway.noRoutedAgents: No agents are routed. Enable an agent on its routing page.
gateway.activityCardDesc: Real routed-request data for this gateway run.
gateway.offConfirmBody: These routed agents will be reverted to Direct mode: {{agents}}

gatewayLogs.title: Gateway Logs
gatewayLogs.help: Live view of the gateway log. Every line carries the request correlation ids (task / attempt), so pasting a task id into the search shows that request's full lifecycle: inbound → route → each attempt (status, latency) → decision → done. Debug adds truncated request/response bodies (never headers, never credentials).
gatewayLogs.searchHint: Search — task id, request id, model…
gatewayLogs.presetDebug: Adds truncated (2 KiB) request/response bodies — enough to diagnose protocol and upstream errors. Bodies contain your code and conversations; never headers or credentials.
gatewayLogs.presetTrace: Everything, including dependency internals. Large logs.
gatewayLogs.emptyHint: Route a request through the gateway, or relax the filters.
gatewayLogs.fullBodiesHint: Log COMPLETE request/response bodies in the debug wire evidence instead of 2 KiB truncated snippets. Large logs; still never headers or credentials.

agentReview.help: Spawn an isolated Pi review session on completed work. It routes through the gateway as the pi:reviewer role, watches the review live, and returns a verdict without touching the main context.
agentReview.newHint: The review runs as a separate Pi session routed to the pi:reviewer policy's provider.
